brief: A three-storey tower: drawers on the bottom storey and open bins on the top storey.

requirements.evidence: Full bases stacked at (0,-1) on levels 0, 1 and 2, held together with snaps and joint bolts.

There are two drawers on level 0, set in half bases on each side of the column: drawer:0#0,0#cut and drawer:0#0,-2#cut. The column's own bottom cell has no drawer, because the configurator won't stack bases on a half base.

requirements.requirement: Open bins on the top storey
requirements.evidence: bin:0,-1,2~hex-bin-full-div3 sits on level 2 with no cover on top, so it is open and split into 3 compartments.

finish.summary: I built a three-storey tower. Its central column is three full hex bases stacked at cell (0,-1), levels 0 to 2. There's no drawer inside the bottom of the column itself, because a drawer only fits on the cut face of a half base and the configurator won't stack anything on a half base. So the bottom storey has two half bases, one each side of the column, and each holds a drawer, pulling out to the north and south. The top storey holds an open full-height bin split into 3 compartments. I added end caps on every open face and bolted the joints together. The collision check came back clear with no issues. The build has 41 parts.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
